title: core
text:
The sandbox
The sandbox keeps tools inside the folders the user opened, called roots. Each path is resolved before it is checked, so .., ~ and symbolic links are judged by where they actually lead. Sandbox does this and raises Unsafe, a HostError, for a path it refuses. Each host keeps one Sandbox and every tool goes through it.
Some paths are refused even when reads outside the roots are allowed. DENY lists them: SSH and cloud credentials, .env files, private keys and similar. denied checks a path against that list, ignoring case, because a case-insensitive disk opens .SSH as .ssh.


source

denied
def denied(
    path,
    patterns:tuple=('*/.ssh/*', '*/.aws/*', '*/.gnupg/*', '*/.config/gcloud/*', '*/.netrc', '*/.git-credentials', '*/.codex/auth.json', '*/.claude/.credentials.json', '*/.env', '*/.env.*', '*/id_rsa*', '*/id_ed25519*', '*.pem', '*.key', '*.p12')
):
Whether path matches one of the refused credential patterns, ignoring case.




source

Unsafe
def Unsafe(
    *args, **kwargs
):
A path that resolves outside every open root, or one refused for safety.


A read tool must not become a way to copy out a key, so denied paths stay refused even with read_outside:

[p for p in ('/home/k/.ssh/id_rsa', '/proj/.env', '/proj/key.pem', '/proj/app.py') if denied(p)]



source

Sandbox
def Sandbox(
    roots:tuple=(), # folders to open for reads and writes; each must already exist
    read_outside:bool=False, # let reads name any path on this machine
    deny:tuple=('*/.ssh/*', '*/.aws/*', '*/.gnupg/*', '*/.config/gcloud/*', '*/.netrc', '*/.git-credentials', '*/.codex/auth.json', '*/.claude/.credentials.json', '*/.env', '*/.env.*', '*/id_rsa*', '*/id_ed25519*', '*.pem', '*.key', '*.p12'), # what `read_outside` still refuses to open
    read_roots:tuple=(), # folders to open for reads only
):
The open folders, and the one place that decides whether a path is inside them.




source

spill
def spill(
    text
):
Save text whole in spill_dir, and return its path.




source

spill_dir
def spill_dir():
The private folder, one per process, where results too long to send whole are saved; every Sandbox may read it and none may write it.


Sandbox(roots) opens folders for reading and writing, and read_roots folders for reading only. check(path) resolves a path, relative to the first root if it is relative, and returns it or raises Unsafe. A path that does not exist yet still resolves, since a tool creating a file needs that; readers pass must_exist=True. reading=True marks a read, which may use read-only roots and read_outside. covers and reads test a path against the two kinds of root, add_root and drop_root open and close folders, root_of names the root holding a path, and bare and under handle a file name given by a person or a model.
A result too long to send whole can be saved with spill, which writes it to the folder spill_dir names and returns the path. Every sandbox may read that folder, so the model can page through the full result with view_file, and none may write to it.

tmp = TemporaryDirectory()
root = Path(tmp.name).resolve()/'proj'
(root/'pkg').mkdir(parents=True)
(root/'pkg'/'a.py').write_text('x = 1\n')

sb = Sandbox([root])
sb.check('pkg/a.py').name, sb.check('pkg/new.py').name, sb.covers(root/'pkg'), sb.root_of('pkg/a.py') == root

Resolving before checking is what stops a symbolic link from escaping: checking the unresolved path would accept link/secret.txt because it looks inside the root. With no open folders nothing resolves, so a host cannot be tricked into reading /etc/passwd.

outside = Path(tmp.name).resolve()/'outside'
outside.mkdir()
(outside/'secret.txt').write_text('token\n')
(root/'link').symlink_to(outside, target_is_directory=True)

test_fail(lambda: sb.check('link/secret.txt'), contains=SANDBOX)        # a symlink out
test_fail(lambda: sb.check('../outside/secret.txt'), contains=SANDBOX)  # .. traversal
test_fail(lambda: sb.check(outside/'secret.txt'), contains=SANDBOX)     # an absolute path elsewhere
test_fail(lambda: sb.check('pkg/new.py', must_exist=True), contains='no such file')
test_fail(lambda: Sandbox().check('/etc/passwd'), contains=NO_ROOTS)    # nothing open, nothing readable

read_outside=True widens reads only. Writes must still land in an open folder, and credential paths are always refused.

lax = Sandbox([root], read_outside=True)
lax.check(outside/'secret.txt', reading=True).name

Open folders never nest. Opening a parent closes the roots inside it, and opening a folder already covered changes nothing, so each file is walked and indexed once.

sb2 = Sandbox([root/'pkg', root])                         # a folder and its parent, opened together
[r.name for r in sb2.roots]

bare refuses a name that is really a path, such as ../../etc. under places a named entry inside a folder without letting it escape.

sb.under('pkg', 'b.py').name, sb.bare('b.py')

title: core
text:
Clipping
Long results have to be cut to fit the budget, and the cut should tell the model what it missed. clip shortens a string to n characters, at a line break when one is close, and appends a note giving how much was shown. The note counts against n. more adds a hint on how to read the rest, and keep=True saves the whole result with spill and names the file in the note. clip_json does the same for JSON while keeping it valid JSON: a list keeps the items that fit plus a last item saying how many more there are, and a dict keeps its plain fields, with the longest strings shortened and a truncated note.


source

clip_json
def clip_json(
    r, n:int=6000
):
r as indented JSON of at most n characters that is still valid JSON, with the whole saved by spill when it does not fit.




source

clip
def clip(
    s, n:int=6000, more:str='', # how to read the rest, when the caller has a way
    keep:bool=False, # save the whole with `spill` and name the file, for a result nothing can page
):
Truncate a tool result to n chars, its note included, whenever n is longer than the note.



print(clip('one\ntwo\nthree\nfour\nfive\n', 12))


import re


test_eq(clip('short', 12), 'short')
five = 'one\ntwo\nthree\nfour\nfive\n' * 3
test_eq(clip(five, 60).splitlines()[0], 'one')
assert len(clip(five, 60)) <= 60, 'the note counts against the budget'
kept = clip(five, 60, keep=True)
saved = Path(re.search(r'saved to (\S+?);', kept).group(1))
test_eq(saved.read_text(), five)
assert len(kept) <= 200 and 'view_file' in kept
report = {'undo': 'u1', 'head': 'abc123', 'branches': [f'branch-{i}' for i in range(200)]}
small = json.loads(clip_json(report, 500))                     # still a document a harness can parse
test_eq((small['undo'], small['head'], 'branches' in small), ('u1', 'abc123', False))
test_eq(json.loads(Path(re.search(r'saved to (\S+?);', small['truncated']).group(1)).read_text()), report)
test_eq(json.loads(clip_json({'undo': 'u1'})), {'undo': 'u1'})
long_result = clip_json({'undo': 'u1', 'result': 'r' * 5000, 'branches': ['b']}, 600)   # a long plain field is shortened, not kept whole
assert len(long_result) <= 600 and json.loads(long_result)['undo'] == 'u1', long_result
commits = [{'sha': f'{i:07d}', 'subject': 'x' * 40} for i in range(100)]
log = clip_json(commits, 800)                                    # a list stays a list: what fits, then a note
assert len(log) <= 800 and isinstance(json.loads(log), list) and 'more' in json.loads(log)[-1], log[-200:]
test_eq(clip('hello', 5), 'hello')
assert clip('hello', 0).startswith('h') and '1 of 5' in clip('hello', 0)   # a zero or negative budget
assert clip('hello', -200).startswith('h')

clip_lines renders a list of lines within n characters and says which line to continue from, which is how view_file pages through a file. more is the hint, and {next} in it is replaced by the next line number. empty is returned for an empty list. A single line longer than the budget is cut by characters, and the note gives its length but no line to resume from.


source

clip_lines
def clip_lines(
    lines, start:int=1, n:int=6000, more:str='', empty:str='(nothing)'
):
Render lines within n chars, the note included whenever n is longer than the note, and say which line to resume from.



print(clip_lines([f'def f{i}(): pass' for i in range(20)], n=200, more='read from line {next}'))


test_eq(clip_lines([], empty='(no matches)'), '(no matches)')
test_eq(clip_lines(['a', 'b'], n=100), 'a\nb')
long = clip_lines(['x' * 500], n=200)
assert long.startswith('x' * 100) and '500 chars' in long and len(long) <= 200, long
paged = clip_lines([f'line {i}' for i in range(100)], n=200, more='read from line {next}')
assert len(paged) <= 200 and 'read from line' in paged, paged
hinted = clip_lines(['x' * 50] * 40, n=1000, more='m' * 600)        # a long hint is reserved whole, not capped at half the budget
assert len(hinted) <= 1000 and hinted.endswith('m]'), len(hinted)

title: core
text:
Edits
A model sends edits as lists, because the tool schemas declare them as arrays, and a harness may pass a stray JSON string through. cmds parses commands for exhash, the hash-addressed editor, into the tuples it expects. edits parses exact-text replacements. Both reject input they cannot read with an error that names the shape wanted.


source

cmds
def cmds(
    commands
):
Parse exhash commands, as JSON or lists, into the tuples exhash expects, nested lists included.



cmds('[["12|a1b2|", "s", "old", "new"], ["30|9f3c|", "a", "appended"]]')


test_eq(cmds([['1|ab|', 'd']]), [('1|ab|', 'd')])
test_fail(lambda: cmds('{"not": "a list"}'), contains='must be a JSON list')
test_fail(lambda: cmds('["bare string"]'), contains='must be an array')

edits accepts a list of {oldText, newText} dicts, a list of [old, new] pairs, or a single dict. A JSON string of any of those is still accepted in this release. apply_edits applies them to a text. Each oldText must appear exactly once, and the edits must not overlap. Otherwise it raises a ValueError naming the edit and how to fix it: give the exact text, add surrounding lines when a match is ambiguous, or merge overlapping edits.


source

apply_edits
def apply_edits(
    text, es
):
Apply exact-text edits to text, or raise saying which one is wrong and why.




source

edits
def edits(
    es
):
{'oldText','newText'} dicts or [old, new] pairs, as a list; a JSON string of either still parses this release.



before = 'def greet(name):\n    return "hello " + name\n'
after = apply_edits(before, edits([{'oldText': 'hello', 'newText': 'howdy'}]))
after


test_eq(edits([{'oldText': 'a', 'newText': 'b'}]), [('a', 'b')])
test_eq(edits([['a', 'b']]), [('a', 'b')]); test_eq(edits({'oldText': 'a', 'newText': 'b'}), [('a', 'b')])
test_eq(edits('[{"oldText": "a", "newText": "b"}]'), [('a', 'b')])            # a string still parses this release
test_fail(lambda: edits('not json'), contains='list of {"oldText"')
test_fail(lambda: edits([{'old_text': 'a', 'new_text': 'b'}]), contains="'oldText' and 'newText'")
test_fail(lambda: edits([['a']]), contains='[old, new]')
test_fail(lambda: edits(3), contains='list of')
try: apply_edits(before, [('', 'x')])
except ValueError as e: assert 'oldText is empty' in str(e) and 'create_file' not in str(e), e   # the message is one both editors can carry
test_eq(after, 'def greet(name):\n    return "howdy " + name\n')

Here are the three refusals on real text. Each message tells the model how to correct the edit, not only that it failed.

refusals = [lambda: apply_edits(before, [('name', 'who')]), lambda: apply_edits(before, [('nowhere', 'x')]), lambda: apply_edits(before, [('def greet', 'def hi'), ('greet(name)', 'hi(n)')])]
for r in refusals:
    try: r()
    except Exception as ex: print(host_err(ex))

diff_text makes the unified diff that edit tools return and that approval prompts show a person.


source

diff_text
def diff_text(
    before, after, path:str='file'
):
A unified diff from before to after, labelled with path.



print(diff_text(before, after, 'greet.py'))


assert '-    return "hello " + name' in diff_text(before, after)
assert diff_text(before, before) == ''

title: core
text:
Which tools write
An application usually asks a person before a tool changes something. @writes marks a tool as one that does, and is_write checks the mark. WRITE_TOOLS lists the same tools by name, for a caller that only has a name; the tests check that the two agree. @acts and has_effect mark tools that act without writing a file the user owns, such as running an API call or starting a watch, and ACTING_TOOLS names them. Approval does not gate these, but a sub-agent told not to act loses them too. The git tools are listed in GIT_READ_TOOLS and GIT_WRITE_TOOLS.
@summary attaches a function that turns a call’s arguments into the one line a person reads after the tool runs, such as “Edit pkg/a.py”. summarise produces that line for a tool or a bare tool name, falling back to name(arg=value, ...). It finds summaries for bare names in SUMMARIES, which shalya.tools fills when it is imported. one_line squeezes any value onto one short line.

):
The imperative one-liner for a call: what a person would say they just did.




source

summary

    fn
):
Mark the one line a person reads after this tool runs. fn is given the call’s arguments.




source

one_line

One line of a value, short enough to sit in a list.




source

Whether tool t acts without writing a user file, the kind of effect approval does not gate.




source

Mark a tool that acts without writing a file the user owns.




source

Whether t is a tool that changes something.

    f

Mark tool f as one that changes something, so an approval step can put it in front of a person.



@writes
def create_file(path, text): return f'wrote {path}'
def view_file(path): return 'contents'
is_write(create_file), is_write(view_file)


test_eq(is_write(create_file), True)
test_eq(is_write(view_file), False)
test_eq(create_file.__name__ in WRITE_TOOLS, True)
test_eq(sorted(GIT_TOOLS), sorted(set(GIT_READ_TOOLS) | GIT_WRITE_TOOLS))
test_eq(GIT_READ_TOOLS, ('git_status', 'git_divergence', 'git_diff', 'git_log'))
assert {'watch', 'research', 'inspect_python'} <= ACTING_TOOLS and not ({'watch_url', 'set_reminder'} & ACTING_TOOLS)
assert 'edit_file' in WRITE_TOOLS and 'watch' not in WRITE_TOOLS

title: skills
text:
Skills come from two sources. A pyskill is a Python module whose docstring is the skill, published by an installed package (see pyskills). A SKILL.md file is a markdown file in a skills folder, in the Agent Skills layout. Both become a Skill, with a name, a source, a description, and where it came from so a person can go and read it.
A Skill holds a loader for its body, not the body, so finding skills does not read every file. When no description is given, it is the body’s first paragraph on one line.
GROUP is the entry-point group installed packages publish pyskills under. EXTRA_MODULES lists modules that are skills but do not publish one. MAX_SKILL_CHARS caps the length of a skill body sent to the model.

GROUP, EXTRA_MODULES, MAX_SKILL_CHARS

('pyskills', ('exhash.skill',), 20000)



test_eq(GROUP, 'pyskills')
test_eq(EXTRA_MODULES, ('exhash.skill',))
test_eq(MAX_SKILL_CHARS, 20_000)



source


def Skill(
    name:str, source:str, description:str='', where:str='', _text:object=None
)->None:
One skill: its name, where it came from, when it applies, and a way to load its full text.




source


def describe(
    text, mx:int=300
):
A one-line description from a skill body: its first paragraph, collapsed.



describe('''Search the web and read results into durable memory.

Use it when a question needs pages nobody has read yet.''')

'Search the web and read results into durable memory.'



test_eq(describe(''), '')
test_eq(describe('one\ntwo\n\nthree'), 'one two')
test_eq(len(describe('x ' * 400)), 300)

def explodes(): raise FileNotFoundError('SKILL.md')
broken = Skill('gone', 'md', _text=explodes)
s.text(), broken.text()

('the whole body', 'could not read skill gone: FileNotFoundError: SKILL.md')



test_eq(s.text(), 'the whole body')
assert broken.text().startswith('could not read skill gone'), broken.text()

test_eq(len(big.text()), MAX_SKILL_CHARS + len('\n…[500 more chars]'))
test_eq(s.dict()['where'], 'nbs/SKILL.md')

text:
Where skills come from
Installed packages publish pyskills under the pyskills entry-point group. A module’s description comes from its docstring, and Python offers no way to read a docstring without importing the module, so discovery imports each pyskill module once. A module with an empty docstring is skipped.


source

mod_skill
def mod_skill(
    name, modpath
):
A Skill for a module, without importing it until someone asks for the body.



assert _mod_skill is mod_skill   # the old name still imports
assert _describe is describe

exhash ships a skill module and is a dependency of shalya, so discovery always finds at least one real pyskill.

found = _pyskills()
[(s.name, s.source, s.where) for s in found]

[('editskill', 'pyskill', 'fastcore.editskill'),
 ('rgapi', 'pyskill', 'rgapi.skill'),
 ('ghapi', 'pyskill', 'ghapi.skill'),
 ('kosha', 'pyskill', 'kosha.skill'),
 ('exhash', 'pyskill', 'exhash.skill'),
 ('skill', 'pyskill', 'nbdev.skill'),
 ('skill', 'pyskill', 'pyskills.skill'),
 ('skill', 'pyskill', 'llmsurgery.skill'),
 ('fastcdp', 'pyskill', 'fastcdp.skill'),
 ('dlgskill', 'pyskill', 'aidialog.dlgskill'),
 ('vishalakshi', 'pyskill', 'vishalakshi.skill'),
 ('coding_patterns', 'pyskill', 'ramabana.coding_patterns'),
 ('theory', 'pyskill', 'ramabana.theory'),
 ('write_docs', 'pyskill', 'ramabana.write_docs'),
 ('write_prose', 'pyskill', 'ramabana.write_prose')]



assert any(s.where == 'exhash.skill' for s in found), [s.where for s in found]
ex = next(s for s in found if s.where == 'exhash.skill')
assert ex.description, 'a pyskill with no description should have been dropped'
assert len(ex.text()) > 100, len(ex.text())

SKILL.md files are looked for in a list of folders, from lowest to highest precedence, so that a later folder’s skill replaces an earlier one with the same name. skill_dirs returns the list. It starts with the skills folder inside learned, for skills a tool wrote rather than a person, then the application’s config folder cfg, then ~/.agents/skills for a person’s own skills, then .leela/skills and .agents/skills in each project root. A project can therefore replace what a person set up for themselves, and a skill a tool learned replaces an installed pyskill but loses to every folder a person writes.
The read_skill tool reads the same installed skill that discovery found through the pyskills entry point:

from shalya.host import LocalHost
from shalya.skills import discover
from shalya.tools import skill_tools


installed_skills = discover()
installed_host = LocalHost(index=False)
installed_read = {t.__name__: t for t in skill_tools(installed_host, lambda: installed_skills)}['read_skill']
installed_exhash = next(s for s in installed_skills if s.where == 'exhash.skill')
installed_body = installed_read(installed_exhash.name)
assert installed_body.startswith(f'<skill name="{installed_exhash.name}"')
assert len(installed_body) > 100 and 'exhash' in installed_body.lower()

Where SKILL.md files are looked for, in increasing precedence: learned first, then the user’s, then each project’s.

['/home/k/.config/leela/skills',
 '/Users/71293/.agents/skills',

test_eq(ds[0], '/cfg/skills')

A skills folder follows the Agent Skills layout: one folder per skill holding a SKILL.md, whose optional frontmatter gives the name and description. Without frontmatter the folder name is the skill’s name and the first paragraph its description.

skill_index renders the block that goes into the system prompt: a heading, a line telling the agent to call read_skill(name) before doing the work a skill covers, and one line per skill with its name and description, never its body. text:
Extensions
An extension is a Python file a user drops in an extensions folder. It defines setup(reg), and through reg, a Registry, it may add tools, skills and slash commands, hook lifecycle events, and replace the approval policy. That is all a Registry offers: it gives an extension no access to the model, the engine or the conversation history.
EVENTS lists the lifecycle events an extension may hook, such as before_tool and after_turn. Hooking any other name raises an error, so a typo cannot silently hook nothing.

EVENTS

('before_turn',
 'after_turn',
 'before_tool',
 'after_tool',
 'compact',
 'approval')



test_eq(EVENTS, ('session_start', 'before_turn', 'after_turn', 'before_tool', 'after_tool', 'stop', 'compact', 'approval', 'background_done', 'watch'))
test_eq(len(set(EVENTS)), len(EVENTS))

load

    reg, roots:tuple=(), cfg:NoneType=None, project:bool=False, paths:tuple=()

Run each extension file and call its setup(reg), recording in reg.notes what each added or why it failed.

Registry
def Registry(
    host:NoneType=None, agent:NoneType=None

What an extension’s setup(reg) may add: tools, skills, commands, hooks and an approval policy.

shell_hooks

    reg, path
):
Register the hooks a hooks.json lists: [{event, match, command}].


load(reg, roots, cfg) runs every .py file in the extension folders (ext_dirs) whose name does not start with _, plus any files or folders given in paths, and calls its setup(reg). It adds one line per file to reg.notes: what the file registered, or why it failed to load. It also registers the shell hooks listed in <cfg>/hooks.json (shell_hooks).
A hook may return a value. fire(event, ...) runs the event’s hooks in registration order and returns their return values, so a before_tool hook can return a reason to deny the call or replacement arguments, and an after_tool hook a rewritten result. A hook that raises is recorded in reg.notes and skipped. A shell hook is a command listed in hooks.json as {event, match, command}, where match is a glob on the tool name. It receives the event as JSON on standard input and may answer with a JSON object on standard output holding deny, args or result. Anything else it prints is ignored.
A real extension, with a real setup(reg), loaded from disk, alongside a file that fails to load and one with no setup:

extdir = tmp/'extensions'
extdir.mkdir()
(extdir/'wc.py').write_text('''
def setup(reg):
    @reg.tool
    def word_count(path: str) -> str:
        "How many words are in a file."
        return str(len(open(path).read().split()))
    reg.command('wc', lambda agent, arg: 'counted ' + arg, help='count words')
    reg.skill('house-style', 'Dense lines. Short names.', 'How code is written here.')
''')
(extdir/'helpers.py').write_text('SHARED = 1\n')
(extdir/'boom.py').write_text('raise RuntimeError("no")\n')
reg = load(Registry(), cfg=tmp)
reg.notes

['boom.py: failed to load (RuntimeError: no)',
 'helpers.py: loaded, no setup()',
 'wc.py: 1 tool(s), 1 skill(s), 1 command(s)']



test_eq([t.__name__ for t in reg.tools], ['word_count'])
test_eq(list(reg.commands), ['wc'])
test_eq([s.name for s in reg.skills], ['house-style'])
test_eq(reg.skills[0].text(), 'Dense lines. Short names.')
test_eq(reg.tools[0](str(extdir/'helpers.py')), '3')          # the tool really runs
assert any('helpers.py: loaded, no setup()' in n for n in reg.notes), reg.notes
assert any(n.startswith('boom.py: failed to load') for n in reg.notes), reg.notes


(tmp/'hooks.json').write_text(json.dumps([
    {'event': 'before_tool', 'match': 'run_*',
     'command': "python3 -c 'import sys, json; d = json.load(sys.stdin); print(json.dumps({\"deny\": \"no rm\"}) if \"rm\" in d[\"args\"][2][\"command\"] else \"logged\")'"},
    {'event': 'nonsense', 'command': 'true'}]))
reg = load(Registry(), cfg=tmp)
test_eq(reg.fire('before_tool', None, 'run_shell', {'command': 'rm -rf x'}), ['no rm'])
test_eq(reg.fire('before_tool', None, 'run_shell', {'command': 'ls'}), [None])
test_eq(reg.fire('before_tool', None, 'view_file', {}), [None])
assert any(n.endswith('1 hook(s)') or 'skipped' in n for n in reg.notes), reg.notes
test_eq(reg.drop_loaded().hooks['before_tool'], [])

Reloading re-reads the extension files, and must not throw away what the running program registered since. load records which registrations came from the files (mark and mark_loaded), and drop_loaded removes exactly those and keeps the rest. loaded says whether the files are currently loaded.

live = load(Registry(), cfg=tmp)
def live_tool(x: str) -> str: return x
live.tool(live_tool); live.command('mine', lambda a, arg: arg); live.on('after_tool', print)
live.drop_loaded()
[t.__name__ for t in live.tools], list(live.commands), len(live.hooks['after_tool']), live.loaded


test_eq([t.__name__ for t in live.tools], ['live_tool'])   # the file's word_count went, mine stayed
test_eq(list(live.commands), ['mine'])
test_eq(len(live.hooks['after_tool']), 1)
test_eq([s.name for s in live.skills], [])
test_eq(live.loaded, False)
load(live, cfg=tmp)                                       # the files come back on the next read
test_eq([t.__name__ for t in live.tools], ['live_tool', 'word_count'])
live.drop_loaded()                                        # and a second round is not lossy
test_eq([t.__name__ for t in live.tools], ['live_tool'])
test_eq(Registry().drop_loaded().tools, [])               # never loaded: nothing to take back

Hooking an unknown event raises an error:

test_fail(lambda: reg.on('before_lunch', print), contains='unknown event')

A failing hook is recorded in notes and does not end the turn. Its result is left out of what fire returns.

fired = []
reg.on('before_turn', lambda **kw: 1/0)
reg.on('before_turn', lambda **kw: fired.append(kw))
reg.fire('before_turn', prompt='hello'), fired, reg.notes[-1]

(1,
 [{'prompt': 'hello'}],
 'before_turn hook failed: ZeroDivisionError: division by zero')



test_eq(fired, [{'prompt': 'hello'}])
test_eq(reg.fire('before_turn', prompt='again'), [None])
assert reg.notes[-1].startswith('before_turn hook failed'), reg.notes[-1]

An extension may replace the approval policy, the function that decides whether a tool call goes ahead. The last one registered wins, and with none registered approve is None.

@reg.approval
def approve_reads(tool, **kw): return not tool.startswith('write_')
reg.approve, reg.approve('view_file'), reg.approve('write_file')

(<function __main__.approve_reads(tool, **kw)>, True, False)



test_eq(reg.approve.__name__, 'approve_reads')
test_eq(reg.approve('view_file'), True)
test_eq(reg.approve('write_file'), False)
test_eq(Registry().approve, None)                         # nothing registered approves everything

Extension folders inside a project load only with project=True. Cloning a repository never runs its code.

test_eq([str(p) for p in ext_dirs(roots=['/proj'], cfg='/cfg', project=True)][-1],
        '/proj/.leela/extensions')
